notes.title: Developer's Note [#9]

Hello from the dev team!
For our ninth update of the development process, we will share collections of "Tokyo Food" pixel arts that were posted on social media! The series consists of 12 foods that represent(?) Tokyo, so we have archived them on this page!

Pixel art illustrated by ZIMA (@pixel_zima)
https://x.com/pixel_zima
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/12bdca4e47eb59f039190ba67be127df6d261d4d.png[/img]

[1. Hamburger]
Lunch time with a creamy avocado burger and lemon soda!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/1cfc57bfc80fe9b4cf62f863ddb4e6a4422845af.gif[/img]

[2. Ramen]
Soy sauce ramen is a taste of Tokyo. Have some gyoza with it too!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/c47eb10cfee3a71e2f58a0861413e5b71757cc54.gif[/img]

[3. Curry]
It has been in Japan for about 150 years and is now so well established that it's considered a national food of Japan!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/55b72fe1272062694b325a21a9f5cb32e04082fd.gif[/img]

[4. Sushi]
Tokyo has many places to enjoy sushi, from casual sushi-go-rounds to upscale sushi restaurants!

[5. Pancake]
From among deserts this time we have pancakes! The colorful toppings are a hit with girls!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/ee98ca5201788d118008e8bae7f23e46830522b7.gif[/img]

[6. Toshi-Koshi-Soba]
New Year's Eve is finally here! These big shrimp are going to be such a feast!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/738abbd21d53134937ccb76b525016e975c74e5a.gif[/img]

[7. Parfait]
When it comes to parfaits, you can enjoy a variety of ingredients at the same time♡
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/799b07d72b2a9bd588666738505cdcd1a6c0b23b.gif[/img]

[8. Yakiniku]
The joy of grilling meat.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/b6b8f746521302e2a989ce2ab13f9ced4e056c6e.gif[/img]

[9. Omu-Rice]
A familiar menu item in a casual diner! The lovely ketchup heart is also a classic!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/74028b053a9c3429b052885012adf762a2013b8d.gif[/img]

Napolitan, a Japanese pasta dish, served with a glass of melon soda!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/456dcd91a807283a9c6153ac6aaec9f37837140e.gif[/img]

Traditional Japanese sweets! They come in a variety of motifs and are fun to look at!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/96492c9b7c6b9aeb126d67611a128e2aa83b0683.gif[/img]

A real Japanese breakfast is grilled salmon, rice and miso soup!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/2c23cdba8846e84a94f1b877a306bc21e91e156a.gif[/img]

notes.title: Developer's Note [#7]
notes.notes:
Hello from the dev team!
For our seventh update of the development process, we will share "Tokyo Trip" pixel art that was posted on social media! The series consists of 12 trips, so we have archived them on this page!

[01 Tokyo Tower]
Introducing an iconic location in Tokyo!
There's something magical about Tokyo Tower at night.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/487ec438fbcfdfe33282ef9c6097cfe03827a76e.gif[/img]


[02 Akihabara]
Akihabara is where various cultures are mixed into one. 
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/a02be956a887034367ef17930f7670836377d808.gif[/img]


[03 Marunouchi]
Marunouchi area near Tokyo station has many interesting sights to see.
The illumination is beautiful too.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/5b235fa4214e6c865067bc43c631c4ccabfc68aa.gif[/img]


[04 Kaminarimon]
The iconic lantern Furai Jinmon at Sensoji. It's amazing when it's lit up at night.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/fd9bed44fdd072ba47ac5ea54bac7cb92f5c0264.gif[/img]


[05 Metropolitan Government]
Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bldg. is 243m offering a nice view of Tokyo.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/7866ed883eaf277242361c76fe65fa0b44359a50.gif[/img]


[06 Ueno Park]
Ueno Park is a city park in Japan with over 140 years of history. It's also known for its beautiful cherry blossoms.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/07046b0bb7508f58602192a1b386f6e5dd71a9e5.gif[/img]


[07 Ryogoku Kokugikan]
Ryogoku Kokugikan is famous for sumo and is well-known to Japanese people.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/9e463ceb76200d1adaa862c4d75fcbe6ebeab8cf.gif[/img]


[08 Rainbow Bridge]
Rainbow Bridge is an iconic landmark, part of Tokyo's beautiful nightscape.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/0211cfa4637bf71b9d9d9538bf0e96bdf4540fd7.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/e16731688f00784ac774d5f4b3dc172dea972aaa.gif[/img]

notes.title: Developer's Note [#6]
notes.notes:
Hello from the dev team!
For our sixth update of the development process, we will share info with you about technology testing.

[Physics Object Test]
We plan to place objects with physics such as empty cans on the side of the road to represent urban reality. In this test, we made various objects fall. The way how they bounce around is looks very realistic.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/2e50937adbe11c709ee3d0154f88c708d698d92c.gif[/img]

In this test, we placed a large number of colored balls and checked for interference with the characters! It turned out to be a pretty fun sight! It's quite fun just experimenting by bouncing the ball around. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/daaa10315b0a188fd8cc6517443e4c02cd7208df.gif[/img]

[Cloth Simulation Test]
We are not sure if we will use it or not, but we also tested the cloth simulation available on Unity. It is a strange sight to see a huge black cloth randomly in a town, but we received various suggestions on social media. I hope we can use this knowledge effectively somewhere!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/1b218fedbe69248e26550a0b6e0884a1981d4ee7.gif[/img]

[Visual Test]
Here is a test image of an old LCD monitor-like effect that we made when we were checking out the visual looks. It was fun to make it look like an old handheld video game. It was difficult to add a sense of depth, but we like it because it looks like something you would find in an extra mode after clearing the game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/7edeabf112e780ff41afe2eb4e012cb087272e20.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/fe21294e61735fe1f9014863e01fde9faae94a81.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/83d9c9ce7c35ecf8f8f1a13213cbd5319dde07df.png[/img]

Unity and Unreal Engine are developing more and more interesting technologies! Game development is a process that goes along with the evolution of technology, so we would like to learn various technologies while having at the same time!

notes.title: [Notice Concerning Postponement of the Release Date of "Tokyo Stories"]
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/65476b2c34dcf7ca79041fa4a2d663ddfb8e7262.png[/img]

"Tokyo Stories" was originally scheduled to be released in 2023. Unfortunately, after much consideration we have decided to postpone the release schedule to "to be determined" status. We are very sorry for all the people who have been looking forward to the release of "Tokyo Stories" to be made this year.

Our original plan of the title was to be a rather small project. But as our team worked on the project day by day, we came to a realization that that we had more ideas and contents we wanted to implement in "Tokyo Stories" than we originally had in mind.

It was a difficult decision for us, but at the same time, it was a chance to make the project even better. From the day when we made our first announcement of "Tokyo Stories" last year, we have been encouraged by many positive reactions and opinions we received from everyone. The voices of the community have driven us to be confident in what we were making. We would like to express our thanks for the support that the community have given us over the year.

With our goal of creating a memorable experience for everyone, we are now working together as a team with all our might to develop this project.

We have prepared a small playable version that will be showcased at our booth in the upcoming "BitSummit Let's Go!" and we are hoping you will come and visit us!

We are still working hard to bring "Tokyo Stories" to you, and it will take some time until the full official release. We appreciate your patience and understanding over this matter, and we look forward to your continued support!

"Tokyo Stories" Producer
Yuki Ikeda

notes.title: Developer's Note [#5]
notes.notes:
Hello from the dev team!
For our fifth update of the development process, we will share info with you about the camera system used in the game.

[Fixed Point Camera]
Tokyo Stories will be using a fixed point camera system. Not many modern games use this camera system any more, but it was a common camera view system used in the early PlayStation 1 and 2 era.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/61c2bb352627d1a8bdf605b642c0fd81f8ee5389.gif[/img]

Instead of allowing the camera to be moved about freely, the player's camera view will be fixed in a position, which adds more control for game designers to deliver the intended content to players. By using this system, it allows us to accurately show the wonderful Tokyo city the way we envision it. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/6d14830b9ecafa5ec49f6f20db10fd42af677f54.gif[/img]

[Strengths and Weaknesses of the system]
One of the major benefits of this system is that it allows us to cut down on the time and effort to make models in areas where the players will never be able to see. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/dccb53172f60bc8d5079827d3ff290e4fe891ed5.png[/img]
By focusing our efforts on the details of models seen within the camera view, it raises the overall quality of the entire screen.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/028cbe038e1570b80ae9e25fab3eee08f664c7e5.png[/img]
Being selective on where to spend our effort is very important for a small teamed indie project.


But there is also a downside to this system as when the camera angle switches to another, it often leads to players momentarily losing their bearings. When a single stage contains multiple fixed camera points, we need to be careful to adjust each of those camera points so that it makes a smooth camera transition between each other. In order for the players to focus into the game content itself, it is important that camera transition feels natural and that the players forget that it is even a thing!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/f97911ff894c094ffa0e3d068520a25bf643c49d.gif[/img]

Speaking of fixed point cameras, that reminds me of older games that had remote controller-like movement control. Tokyo Stories is currently designed to use the analogue stick for a more intuitive movement, but it might be fun if we added a classic "remote controller mode" as a little bonus for completing the game once.

notes.title: Developer's Note [#4]
notes.notes:
Hello from the dev team!
For our forth update of the development process, we will share info with you about visual effects used within the map.

[Environmental Effects]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/5105578282b62e468ab5fa4f213a18c74b27bbd9.gif[/img]
The map is not complete yet with just 3D models. It also needs visual effects such as dust-like particles that float around and lighting effects from objects like lights and vending machines. Lighting effect also needs to be adjusted accordingly to put emphasis on the light source. A single screen will contain multiple visual effects by the time when it is completed.

[Plants]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/a925747e6e11e88a65fc6014d025cff31a618692.gif[/img]
Large plants have animations. By intentionally reducing the number of animation frames, it can make it look less like a 3D model. Although not a plant, the flickering neon sign also stands out doesn't?

[Testing Snow Effects]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/e9df75e89a6029ae4b056238138bb1b47b191a10.gif[/img]
Snow map effect we made for testing purposes. We made it in case snow started to fall in Tokyo. One benefit of using 3D is that it is easy to add effects later if we decide to do so.

Movements such as particles and blinking lights make the screen more lively, compensating the static nature of the camera view. There are more effects we want to add to the background and we will share more on that as we continue to make the game!

notes.title: Developer's Note [#3]
notes.notes:
Hello from the dev team!
For our third update of the development process, we will share insight with you about the city of Tokyo where the game is set in!

Although most of our team members work remotely, our team headquarters are in Tokyo. Tokyo is an astonishing city that appeared in many other titles, to a point one may say it is overused. For "Tokyo Stories," we are depicting the other side of Tokyo. 

Unlike the busy main streets of Tokyo, the back alley of the city has a totally different impression. It is like a separate dimension cut out from the crowd. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/466a58bc2140e5c05a52068c5aa6f7658ae89aab.gif[/img]

It may be worth to sit down at a back alley with a drink in hand, or explore it a bit on your own. Don't worry, the city will not reject you. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/25d5a1d41faa14b7ebbb5cde893f568d691c7b23.gif[/img]

On paper, traveling around the city can be done simply by a short ride on the train. However, to actually execute it can be difficult even for us locals living in Tokyo when we have to figure out on what subway station we have to transfer to reach our destination.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/03f199ddc54c427946785103a1e868a847e15049.gif[/img]

Finding a space where you can be alone within the city is like a little discovery that only you can make. Just imagine, what was this place waiting for you to arrive as if time had been standing still?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/ab113eb208c782eb14e669a381110ade89a5efd7.gif[/img]

The Tokyo we want to depict in "Tokyo Stories" is not the famous tourist city of Tokyo. We want to shed more light on the rather forgotten, yet kindly embracing backside of the Tokyo city. We are hoping that "Tokyo Stories" will become an inspiration to players on discovering their new impression towards Tokyo.

notes.title: Developer's Note [#2]
notes.notes:
Hello from the dev team!
For our second update of the development process, we will share with you a little about character designs!

Each character has a theme color to easily distinguish them when made into a pixel art.

[Character.1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/736f090a56018f718f71f332892734eaf9874883.png[/img]
The main character wears an oversized parka and a large pair of sneakers. Her theme color is blue, including her backpack and even her shoelaces! She prefers a dark color scheme that blends into the night, suggesting her personality perhaps?

[Character.2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/96f966b07423a53b523bfaac5ae7afb2db370781.png[/img]
The main character's friend. She wears relatively relaxed outerwear and her iconic flower hair accessory. Her theme color is mainly yellow, but also have other soft colors to complement. Her kindly yet enigmatic impression might be the reason of attracting the main character's attention.

[Character.3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/4bb360bf946323dac0c993f62ff836d82c2e17a4.png[/img]
A young man wearing a rather tight clothes in a casual fashion. His theme color is red, with the collar fur that stands out on his slim-fit coat that he wears in a rough way. Judging by his neck accessories and ear piercings, he seems to display a rather showy taste with his looks.

Lastly, here are some rough sketches: 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/62a2243c03692a5302e7aece2a0f8bf9a12fd683.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/4c4bde0a0cb7c93fb6df729bc045c7f6470744ed.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/36ecb83a3439a1394bf459821d8f035a8a764913.png[/img]
Characters went through many iterations to reach their final design, but we will share more of that at a later time.

Will there be other characters besides these three? What are their names? How old are they?

Next, we'll be sharing about Tokyo where this title will be based in! Make sure to stick around to see the next development process update!

notes.title: Developer's Note [#1]
notes.notes:
Hello from the dev team!
From now on, we are going to occasionally share some behind-the-scenes updates of the development process!

We’ll be posting exclusive content that won’t be shared on social media platforms.

[PixelArt+3D]
This is a breakdown video of the pixel art expression, which is the biggest challenge in the visual aspect of our work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/b7bfc99eba69c8c35ed851232c886d1a8e12883a.gif[/img]

First, we create a rough impression by setting the lighting on the polygonal background model.
Next, we burn the shadows of non-moving parts into a light map and apply a texture to the 3D model.
Then, we enhance the shader lighting and apply a distortion effect to the light-dark boundary.
After that, we pixelate the entire image and apply colour reduction using the colour palette.
Last, we adjust the colours of the entire screen and apply a final brush to complete the process.
(In reality, there are various minor adjustments made.)

Here is a scene from the game that was created using this process:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/c61391599b987e1380fa2a9ad77b5487df32d8e6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43548694/eef66c60fd25fff81c44dc7908631dd28773b065.png[/img]

We'll be sharing more in the future, so make sure to stick around!
